headline: February 29—the bonus day that keeps our calendar aligned with the cosmos
universal_truth: Even our timekeeping systems require adjustment; perfection is an approximation refined over time
fun_facts: A year is actually 365.2422 days—leap years correct the accumulated drift
People born on February 29 are called 'leaplings'—about 5 million worldwide
The Gregorian calendar skips leap years in century years unless divisible by 400
discussion_questions: What would you do with a truly 'bonus' day?
How do you feel about the arbitrariness of our calendar?
What other systems in life require periodic adjustment?

hook.script: Happy Leap Day! This day doesn't exist most years. It's a bonus—an extra 24 hours that keeps our calendar aligned with Earth's actual orbit. Let's explore why we need this correction.

cliff.script: Why can't we just have 365 days every year? What would happen if we ignored the extra fraction?
cliff.prompt: Why do we need leap years?

options.text: Earth's orbit takes 365.2422 days—without correction, seasons would drift; in 700 years, summer would be in December; leap days prevent calendar chaos
options.response: Exactly. That quarter-day adds up. Without leap years, the calendar would slowly disconnect from seasons. Our ancestors figured this out through careful observation.
It's actually astronomy! The tradition exists because the math demands it...

fact1.title: The 400-Year Pattern
fact1.script: Leap year rules are more complex than 'every four years.' Century years like 1900 skip the leap day—unless divisible by 400, like 2000. This fine-tuning keeps us accurate for millennia.

fact2.title: Leaplings
fact2.script: About 5 million people worldwide were born on February 29. They celebrate birthdays on February 28 or March 1 in non-leap years. Some joke they're 'technically' a quarter of their age.

fact3.title: Historical Adjustments
fact3.script: When the Gregorian calendar replaced the Julian in 1582, ten days were skipped to realign with the seasons. People went to sleep October 4 and woke up October 15. Imagine that adjustment!

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Even timekeeping needs correction. Systems drift; adjustments restore alignment. In life too, regular recalibration keeps us on course.

outro.script: That's your leap year lesson. Use this bonus day wisely—it won't come again for four years. What will you do with your extra 24 hours?

growTrack.title: Bonus Day Challenge - Use It Wisely
growTrack.learning_objective: Make intentional use of bonus time
growTrack.activity: It's a bonus day! Do something you've been postponing. Learn something you've been curious about. Reach out to someone you've been meaning to contact. Make this extra day count.
